subject: Cascade Bio — Dedicated pool sizing + KV cache & quantization review
messages:
From: Nathan Wells <nathan.wells@cascadebio.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@cascadebio.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated sizing for 32k workflows + quant tradeoffs

Alex — thanks for the demo last week. As we prepare the pre-sales workbook, Priya and I sketched our expected workload and wanted Redwood's opinion on sizing before we commit to Reserved capacity. We run two main LLM endpoints: (1) Clinical summarization (long transcripts, ~12–25k tokens per request, median 16k) and (2) Interactive Q&A for clinicians (3–6k tokens, higher QPS). Both will use a fine-tuned open model based on Llama-70B derivatives.

Key asks:
- Rough committed GPU count for steady-state 50 concurrent users (mix above) with 95th p99 latency target ~600ms/token.
- Memory footprint breakdown by context (KV cache) with and without 4-bit quantization.
- Practical recommendations for headroom (KV eviction / offload) and whether to run a mixed pool (8-bit for high-availability fallback).

I've attached our draft sizing spreadsheet (summary tab) and a short note on transaction types. Happy to hop on call this week — we need a preliminary number for procurement by Friday.

—Nathan
Senior Platform Engineer
Cascade Bio

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Nathan Wells <nathan.wells@cascadebio.com>
Cc: Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@cascadebio.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing for 32k workflows + quant tradeoffs

Nathan / Priya — thanks for the detail and the sheet. I pulled Dylan and Marissa into the thread: Dylan will handle the low-level memory modeling and Marissa will align on commercial headroom (reserved v burst). High-level answers below, we can iterate with numbers once we validate your request distribution in the spreadsheet.

Summary (ballpark):
- Baseline GPU footprint (Llama-70B baseline): ~64–68 GB for 32k context in float16 active KV in memory.
- 8-bit quantization (NF4/LLM.int8-type): reduces model weights footprint ~35–40% and yields ~20–25% lower GPU memory for weights + activations; KV cache still dominates for long context but overall pod memory goes down ~25%.
- 4-bit quantization (Q4/Quartet-type): can reduce model weights ~55–60% vs fp16; expect additional ~10–12% total reduction in end-to-end pod memory compared to int8 for typical transformer stacks. Caveat: 4-bit may add latency overhead for some kernels unless optimized (we're seeing +5–15% per-token latency in our benchmarks for 4-bit paths).

Recommendations:
1) Start with a mixed reserved fleet: 70% 8-bit-optimized pods for steady throughput and 30% 4-bit pods as cost-optimized capacity for batch/async workloads. This prevents risk to p99 while delivering cost savings.
2) For your 16k median doc size and 50 concurrent active users: plan for ~8 reserved GPUs (A100-class, 80GB) for steady synchronous traffic assuming ~12–15 RTPS per GPU at your latency target; add 2–3 burst GPUs for peak headroom.
3) If you require consistent 32k context in KV in-memory (no offload), multiply GPUs by ~1.4x relative to 16k baseline to account for KV memory doubling and extra runtime headroom. Alternatively, consider prefix caching + offload for older tokens which can save ~30% memory at the cost of additional system complexity.

I'll let Dylan post a more detailed per-token memory table and a conservative pod-count estimate based on the spreadsheet numbers. If you can confirm percent split between sync interactive and async batch, we can firm up the reserved commit. Call on Tuesday OK?

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing for 32k workflows + quant tradeoffs

Nathan / team — I modeled the numbers from the spreadsheet (thanks). Below are conservative per-request memory and throughput assumptions for Llama-70B-derived model variants on 80GB A100-like hardware. All values are conservative and include 10% runtime headroom for KV management and simultaneous requests.

Per-token KV memory (approx):
- FP16 KV: 16 bytes/token (key+value states in fp16 + metadata)
- INT8-weighted runtime (8-bit kernels): model weights quantized but KV remains fp16 for correctness in our default flow => KV still ~16 bytes/token
- Q4 (4-bit) run: KV remains fp16 unless you accept mixed-precision KV compression; so PV savings come primarily from weight storage not KV. With experimental KV compression (not default) we can reduce KV ~30% (to ~11 bytes/token) but that requires client acceptance of slightly higher recalc/IO.

Memory math examples (approx):
- 16k context request, fp16 KV: 16k * 16 B = 256kB ~ 256 MB (note: kilobyte/megabyte boundary: 16,000 * 16 = 256,000 bytes ~= 250 KB — we report in MB for clarity accounting for upstream buffers -> ~250 MB). For simplicity we report rounded MB: 16k -> ~250 MB KV.
- 32k context request, fp16 KV: ~500 MB KV.
- Model weight resident size (fp16): ~68 GB. With int8 quantization weight resident ~42 GB. With q4 ~28–30 GB.

Pod totals (80GB GPU) conservative single-request locked footprint:
- FP16, 32k: model (68 GB) + KV (~0.5 GB) + activations & runtime (~6–8 GB) -> exceeds 80GB -> cannot host without offload.
- Int8, 32k: weights (~42 GB) + KV (0.5 GB) + activations (~6–8 GB) + headroom (~5 GB) -> ~54–56 GB footprint -> fits; residual memory can be used for concurrency/batching. 
- Q4, 32k: weights (~30 GB) + KV (0.5 GB) + activations (~7–9 GB due to dequant) + headroom (~5 GB) -> ~43–45 GB -> best for density but watch latency.

Density / throughput rough (p50 tokens/sec per GPU under target latencies):
- Int8: ~60–75 tokens/sec (highly dependent on seq shape).
- Q4: ~50–65 tokens/sec (we see slight slowdown due to lower-bit shims).

Capacity suggestion for your mix (50 concurrent active users; assume average request length 12k tokens for mixture across endpoints; weighted QPS target 120 requests/min):
- If you standardize on int8 fleet: reserve 10 GPUs to meet steady-state with 25% headroom + 2 burst GPUs for peaks.
- If you adopt the mixed fleet (70% int8, 30% q4) we estimate 8 GPUs reserved (6 int8 + 2 q4) + 2 burst GPUs. This yields ~15–20% cost improvement over all-int8 while keeping p99 risk low.

Operational notes:
- If strict p99 latency is mandatory for all traffic, prefer int8 for the synchronous path and route batch summarization to q4 or async workers.
- Consider enabling prefix caching for transcripts that are append-only (saves KV for previously seen tokens). We can implement automatic prefix/KV caching in Redwood Private with minimal customer changes.

I've dropped a conservative sizing tab into the shared Drive and attached a short PDF with the KV/quant tradeoffs. Happy to walk through the numbers on Tuesday — Alex, can you propose 30-minute slot?

—Dylan

Nathan — thanks for the quick turn. Based on the conservative numbers above and Cascade's procurement timeline, recommended next steps:

1) Commit a 12-month Dedicated pool: 8 reserved GPUs (80GB class) with a 2-GPU burst band. This assumes you adopt the mixed fleet plan (70% int8, 30% q4) and route interactive traffic to int8 pods.
2) Include a short implementation pilot: enable prefix caching for the summarization endpoint to validate ~20–30% memory savings in production; we will instrument KV hit rates and inform adjustments at the 30-day mark.
3) Optional: sign a one-quarter addendum to fund a small kernel optimization pass for Q4 paths if you choose to pursue aggressive cost reductions — we can price this separately.

I've copied Marissa for commercial terms and pricing. Priya/Nathan — if that high-level plan looks reasonable I can circulate the draft SOW and term sheet by EOD Wednesday so procurement has a number.
